sections.title: Pros
sections.narration: Pros first: brings polyphenols when fresh. The bitter, peppery quality is part of the real extra-virgin advantage. Mostly monounsaturated fat identity. That gives it a different fat-quality role from many seed oils and animal fats. Helps carry fat-soluble nutrients. A little oil can make vegetable-heavy meals work better.

sections.title: Cons
sections.narration: Cons next: quality drops with heat, light, and age. The best part of extra virgin olive oil depends on freshness and storage. Extremely energy dense. It is still pure fat, so the calories arrive fast. Easy to overpour without noticing. Free-pouring can quietly add a lot more than intended.

closing.summary: Best bits are fat quality, vitamin E, vitamin K, and polyphenol upside. Weak spots are no carb or protein role, basically no minerals, and easy overpouring. Best for heart health, finishing food, and vegetable-heavy meals because the fat profile is strong, freshness matters, and a small amount can make vegetables work better.
